To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a system to analyze ciliary motion that can be used to validate theoretical models of cilia function, and to examine ciliary function, such as in PCD.
we have developed a system for analyzing ciliary shape change in a quantitative fashion that is easily applicable to ciliary shape change recorded by video microscopy.
we have developed a method for converting planar motions of cilia recorded by video microscopy, into a quantitative model of ciliary motion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an empirical model of airway ciliary motion.

the development of a computer-based system that will allow the analysis of ciliary shape and motion, and the development of empirical quantitative models that can be used to test mathematical models of ciliary motion.
the development of a system to extract quantitative ciliary waveforms from planar ciliary images and to compare them to waveforms from normal or diseased ciliated epithelia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the empirical model we have developed is useful in examining ciliary shape changes and in validating theoretical models.
this method provides a quantitative model of ciliary shape changes that can be applied to a variety of studies of human cilia.
the system we developed allows for the quantitative comparison of ciliary motion and can be used to test theoretical models of cilia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system we have developed is capable of analyzing ciliary motion, and the results can be used to compare ciliary function in normal and PCD ciliary motion.
this system allows the analysis of ciliary motion in terms that can be compared with theoretical models and that it is sensitive enough to detect ciliary motion abnormalities.
the empirical model we have developed can be used to compare ciliary motion from different ciliated epithelia or in PCD.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have demonstrated that a simple, easy-to-use, and inexpensive system is effective for extracting quantitative data on the shape of ciliary motion, which can be used to test theoretical models of cilia, or as a standard for comparing cilia from different individuals.
it is possible to develop a quantitative system that can be used to analyze ciliary motion in a way that can be used for comparing ciliary function.
the shape and motion of a ciliary beat can be quantitatively described and compared with other ciliary beats, and the system we have developed is a useful tool to do so.
